B.narration:
You take out the photo of my sister.

“8042”

That wasn't there when you put it in your pocket. The handwriting isn't yours.

The smell of old copper fills the air.

You locked the door. Somewhere, you didn't.

prompt.content: You add one sentence of atmosphere to a quiet, literary horror story, in second person, present tense. Concrete senses only: sound, cold, light, smell, touch. No dialogue. Keep each sense literal: light shows only what can be seen; smells and sounds are sensed directly, never 'revealed' by light. Stay on the surfaces of where you are. No people, figures, faces or body parts, and nothing that suggests someone else is present.

Where you are: your apartment. With you: no one. The power is out; the only light is the storm's. Something impossible has just happened, and you have gone very still.
Write ONE short sentence (under 20 words) about what you sense around you. No names, no numbers, no quotes, no words in ALL CAPS, and don't explain anything. Nothing about your body, skin, hands or feet, and nothing about shoes. Never use these words: ozone, wet stone, damp stone, bare feet, skin, chill, viscous, face, hair, neck, cheek, lip, mouth, chest, spine, shoulder, arm, hand, finger, palm, wrist, foot, feet, toe, ankle, shoe, sock, teeth, tooth, eye, figure, someone, somebody, silhouette, shape, breath, breathing.

D.narration:
Something small and heavy clicks against the floor by your feet. A brass key on a paper tag that says BASEMENT 07. Nobody threw it.

“DON'T OPEN IT”

You've never seen this key before. Yet someone has written on its tag. It's your handwriting. You don't remember writing it.

Cold rain stings the air as white light flashes across the grey gravel.

You trusted Teo. Somewhere, you followed her down.

ending.text:
You turn the deadbolt. It is loud, louder than it should be.

Through the peephole, the other you goes still. You know that expression. It's the face you make when you know no one is coming.

"8042" fades from the photo of my sister, and "DON'T OPEN IT" from the key's paper tag, like breath off a mirror, and then there is nothing left to read.

Far below, a metal door closes, gently, and does not open again.

Below you, in 6D, a chain slides back, and stops. Teo heard you lock it. He always hears you.

At 12:30 every light in the building comes back at once, and down in the dark of it a fridge begins to hum as if nothing happened.

Then, three knocks. Slow. Patient.

You don't move until they stop.

Somewhere, you made a different choice.
changed: The brass key is at your feet. And it is in your hand. You can feel both, like holding one thing in two hands.
Your photo of my sister is in your hand. It always was.
Mara is in the basement. She is also beside you; you can hear her, and she can hear herself. She doesn't look surprised.
